lines.text: One film. A million people. All pressing play inside the same second.
Do the arithmetic. One ultra-high-definition stream is about fifteen megabits per second. A million of them is fifteen terabits.
So the film is never sent. It is cut into segments, six seconds each, and those are what travel.
Encode every segment more than once, at different bitrates. Same six seconds of story. Three different weights.
Then publish one text file that lists them. That playlist is everything the player is given. It works out the rest itself.
Watch the buffer. When throughput drops, the player asks for a smaller rendition next. The picture softens. It never stops.
Now put copies near people. A million viewers reach a nearby cache. The origin serves that segment once.
Small pieces. Several sizes. One list. Cached close. That is streaming at scale.

bgm.blob: You are never sent the film. It is cut into six-second segments, encoded at several bitrates, listed in one text file, and served from a cache near you.
bgm.arc: The valley (one film, a million people) → Title → The arithmetic (15 Tbps) → Segmentation, the thesis → The bitrate ladder → The manifest (the one dark frame) → Adaptive bitrate on the road → The edge caches at dusk → Takeaway on the hilltop
